note: This sub-site's own flag register. It does NOT write into data/flags.json, which another session owns. Every flag names the official link that settles it, or says plainly that no official source settles it. Flagged items never block the build, by the brief's own instruction.

rows.what: The Week 11 injury report does not exist yet
rows.detail: https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/reg11 serves the Week 10 page (title 'Week 10 of the 2026 Season'). Any page that showed Week 11 designations today would be inventing them.
rows.repo_says: nothing claims Week 11 designations; the capture is labelled Week 10
rows.status: open — cannot be closed by this repository, only by the NFL publishing it

rows.what: Only 2 capture days of the injury report exist, so the 'surprise' cannot be computed
rows.detail: heartbeat.jsonl holds 5 readings over 2 UTC days with an identical canonical hash; 0 designation changes have ever been recorded. The brief's requirement is a timestamped series from Wednesday to kickoff, which needs at least 3 more days per week.
rows.repo_says: data/readiness.json row R5 says '2 capture day(s); 0 designation change(s) recorded' — correct and honest
rows.status: open — needs the capture schedule widened, not a code fix

rows.what: nfl.com prints two different names for the Chiefs' stadium
rows.detail: The game centre's Game Info block prints 'ARROWHEAD STADIUM'. The same site's Week 11 schedule page prints 'GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium' in its hotel link. The pinned feed prints the longer name. Publishing either as 'the official name' without qualification would be a claim the site cannot support.
rows.repo_says: this sub-site publishes 'ARROWHEAD STADIUM' (the game-centre string) and prints the schedule-page variant beside it
rows.status: open — a naming inconsistency on the official site, not resolvable here

rows.what: 'Missing starter' in the depth ladder means two things at once
rows.detail: The generator's slots_missing_starter column adds (a) slots with no available listed player and (b) slots where a backup is pressed into duty. Only 3 of the 41 are type (a); 38 are type (b). A reader who assumed the column meant 'empty slot' would be wrong by 38 slots.
rows.repo_says: the column is published without a definition beside it; this sub-site prints the split and the identity 41 = 38 + 3
rows.status: needs review — a one-line definition beside the column would close it

rows.what: The Cardinals' club code is not consistent across the repository
rows.detail: Official nfl.com pages use 'AZ'. The nflverse feed uses 'ARI'. The committed standings snapshot stores the club as 'AZ'; this session's fixture file, built on the feed's key, uses 'ARI'. A join on the raw code drops the club. The Rams have the same problem (official 'LA', feed 'LAR').
rows.repo_says: no alias map exists and no gate fails an unmapped code
rows.status: open — needs one alias table plus a build gate

rows.what: Four pre-registration registries coexist and are not reconciled
rows.detail: data/preReg/registry.json (3 frozen rules), data/preregistration/registry.json (RULES_v1, 0 strategies), data/prereg/registrations.json (126 entries), data/strat/preregistration.json (31 records). Each has its own registration hash and its own checker. Two different checkers are even named check_preregistration.py and check_preregistration_d4027.py.
rows.repo_says: COORDINATION.md records the fragmentation and states reconciling it is a board decision
rows.official_source: n/a — internal governance, no official source applies
rows.status: needs review — a human must name the authoritative registry

rows.what: The base commit fails its own reproducibility gate for two data files
rows.detail: tools/check_reproducible.py fails on data/readiness.json (a new capture day changed a count from 1 to 2) and data/combined_verification.json (row count 2,899 vs the committed value), because a data-bot commit landed after the last rebuild. Regenerating and committing the rebuilt output closes it; the numbers themselves are correct.
rows.repo_says: the gate fails loudly, which is the intended behaviour
rows.status: fixed by this session — the rebuilt output is committed and the gate passes

rows.what: 18 defaulted values and 2 wrong URLs in this session's own availability table, caught before publication
rows.detail: The first draft of availability.json carried missing_starter = 0 for every club instead of the generator's value, and two chart URLs were typed rather than copied. A field-by-field comparison against data/depth_ladder.json caught it; every value was re-read from the source.
rows.repo_says: the corrected file is published, and the check that caught it is committed as part of brief/verify.py's input set
rows.status: resolved before publication — published here because hiding it would defeat the purpose of the page

rows.what: Two numbers in this session's own reconciliation file were typed rather than computed
rows.detail: The per-club 'changed' flag and the standings tie count were first written by hand. Recomputing them from the two strings moved the identical/changed split from 12/20 to 8/24 and the tie entries from 1 to 2 (one tied game, two clubs).
rows.repo_says: both are now computed and the page shows the computed values

rows.what: Nothing can confirm that a listed backup actually played
rows.detail: No official inactive list, Game Book or snap-count capture exists in the repository for Week 10. 20 inactive rows exist for Week 9 only, 8 of them emergency quarterbacks. The 38 'backup projected to start' slots are therefore depth-chart projections, not observations.
rows.repo_says: data/readiness.json row R7 says '0 of 137 played 2026 games archived'
rows.status: open — needs the Game Book archive (the brief's own route)

rows.what: No official price exists for any market, so no ROI is against an official number
rows.detail: The NFL publishes no odds. Every price in the repository comes from a pinned third-party parse, and every ROI therefore measures skill against a market that has not been officially confirmed.
rows.repo_says: the price source is labelled on every page that prints a price
rows.official_source: n/a — no official odds page exists
rows.status: open — needs the price-data policy decision (Q10), not a capture

rows.what: The site has four competing landing pages and ~194 HTML pages
rows.detail: index.html (pipeline/gen_site.py), dashboard.html (governance registers), web/dashboard.html, room/index.html, plus lab/, research/, verified-lab/, docs/, referee/, strat/, prereg/, shadow/, capture/ and review-room/ sub-sites. Nothing is wrong with any of them; a reader has no single front door, and the header nav carries 38 entries.
rows.repo_says: tools/check_reachability.py passes because every page is reachable from somewhere
rows.status: needs review — this session publishes brief/ as one clean front door and links the rest, rather than deleting anyone's work

counts.note: computed from the rows by the build, not typed
